To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gro EL gene is a good example of convergent evolution and that this gene transfer has shaped the evolution of phototrophic organisms.

the two chaperone genes gro EL and gro ES were transferred from the cyanobacterial progenitor of plastid into the nucleus of eukaryotic host cells and that the genes have been lost or retained by the eukaryotic lineage.

(1) the evolution of gro EL in phototroph eukaryotes is a result of differential gene transfers, duplications and targeting events; (2) gro EL homologs are not maintained in all evolutionary lines, but are lost, duplicated and relocated; and (3) the evolution of two distinct gro EL homologous genes is an example of convergent evolutionary processes in different eukaryotic lines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of a chaperone protein, which is essential for the maintenance of photosynthetic organisms.
the evolutionary history of a chaperon protein that was introduced into eukaroytic genomes by a progenitor plastid.
the evolutionary history of genes that are involved in photosynthesis and are of fundamental significance to the survival of phototrophs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gro EL genes have been maintained in all phototrophic eucaryotes, but not in all phototrophs.
gro EL homologous sequences have been transferred from the cyanobacterial endosymbiont into the nucleus of the primary endosymbiotic host and the secondary endosymbiotic hosts.
the gro EL genes have been transferred to the nucleus in the primary and secondary endocytobioses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of gro EL homologue genes in eukaryotes is shaped by the evolutionary processes of gene transfer, gene deletion, gene duplication, gene fusion and gene relocation.
gro EL homologs have been lost in many lineages, but have been duplicated in others, and that these genes have been relocated to the nucleus in some cases.
gro EL is a model for the study of gene transfers and convergences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genome distribution of genes introduced into photobionts during endosymbiosis is not random.
while the majority of genes are lost during endosymbiosies, some genes are maintained and undergo lineage specific evolutionary processes.
gene transfers, gene deletions, and gene duplications are not independent events but are interdependent and co-occurring events.
